name: core
description: The curated core grammar pack, written fresh for 屠つ. Explanations are original, and so are the examples except in the entries added 2026-10-17, which use Tatoeba sentences (CC BY 2.0 FR, credited on the About page; sentence numbers in local documentation). Nothing is copied from Imabi or Tae Kim: they are all-rights-reserved and may only be linked (project notes §8). A larger pack derived from the CC-licensed hanabira material is a separate, later import. Every `match` rule uses surfaces confirmed against real ichiran-cli output — Ichiran merges a great deal (ことができる and はずです each arrive as ONE token), so rules are deliberately conservative and are extended only once a surface has been observed.

patterns.title: Topic marker は
patterns.explanation: Marks what the sentence is about, often in contrast with something else. Written は but pronounced wa.

examples.japanese: 私は学生です。
examples.english: I am a student.

patterns.title: Subject marker が
patterns.explanation: Marks the subject, and picks it out as new or as the specific one that does the action.

examples.japanese: 猫がいる。
examples.english: There is a cat.

patterns.title: Object marker を
patterns.explanation: Marks the direct object — what the action is done to.

examples.japanese: 水を飲む。
examples.english: Drink water.

patterns.title: に
patterns.explanation: Marks where something ends up, when it happens, or who receives it.

examples.japanese: 東京に行く。
examples.english: Go to Tokyo.

patterns.title: で
patterns.explanation: Marks where an action happens, or what it is done by or with.

examples.japanese: 家で食べる。
examples.english: Eat at home.

patterns.title: と
patterns.explanation: Joins nouns as a complete list, or marks who something is done together with.

examples.japanese: 友達と行く。
examples.english: Go with a friend.

patterns.title: から
patterns.explanation: Marks the starting point in space or time. After a clause it gives the reason.

examples.japanese: 駅から歩く。
examples.english: Walk from the station.

patterns.title: まで
patterns.explanation: Marks the limit something reaches — as far as, or until.

examples.japanese: 駅まで歩く。
examples.english: Walk as far as the station.

patterns.title: より
patterns.explanation: Marks what something is being compared against — than.

examples.japanese: 思ったより安い。
examples.english: Cheaper than I thought.

patterns.title: の
patterns.explanation: Links two nouns: possession, or one describing the other. Also turns a clause into a noun.

examples.japanese: 私の本。
examples.english: My book.

patterns.title: も
patterns.explanation: Adds the sense of too, also, or even. It replaces は and が rather than stacking with them.

examples.japanese: これもいい。
examples.english: This one is fine too.

patterns.title: か
patterns.explanation: Turns a statement into a question. Between nouns it means or.

patterns.title: ね
patterns.explanation: Invites the listener to agree — isn't it, right?

patterns.title: よ
patterns.explanation: Presses the point, telling the listener something they may not know.

patterns.title: へ
patterns.explanation: Marks the direction something heads in. Written へ but pronounced e.

patterns.title: や
patterns.explanation: Joins nouns as an incomplete list — this, that, and others.

examples.japanese: 本や雑誌。
examples.english: Books, magazines, and so on.

patterns.title: には
patterns.explanation: に with the topic は over it: singles out the target for contrast or emphasis.

examples.japanese: 彼には時間がない。
examples.english: He, for his part, has no time.

patterns.title: では
patterns.explanation: で with the topic は over it: as for that place or that means, in contrast with others.

patterns.title: とは
patterns.explanation: Sets up what a word means, or marks who something was done with in contrast.

patterns.title: にも
patterns.explanation: に with も: to that one as well.

patterns.title: ので
patterns.explanation: Gives the reason as a plain fact. Softer and less argumentative than から. Casually 〜んで.

examples.japanese: 安いので買った。
examples.english: I bought it because it was cheap.

patterns.title: のに
patterns.explanation: Although — and usually with a note of surprise or complaint that it turned out that way.

patterns.title: けど
patterns.explanation: But, though. The everyday spoken form of けれども.

examples.japanese: 安いけど買わない。
examples.english: It's cheap, but I won't buy it.

patterns.title: 〜ながら
patterns.explanation: Doing one thing while doing another at the same time.

examples.japanese: 読みながら歩く。
examples.english: Walk while reading.

patterns.title: 〜ことができる
patterns.formation: dictionary form + ことができる
patterns.explanation: Can do it — stating the ability plainly, a little more formally than the potential form.

examples.japanese: 見ることができる。
examples.english: It is possible to see it.

patterns.title: 〜かもしれない
patterns.explanation: It might be so. Leaves real room for it not to be.

examples.japanese: 雨かもしれない。
examples.english: It might rain.

patterns.title: 〜ことがある
patterns.explanation: After a past form: have done it before. After a dictionary form: it happens sometimes.

patterns.title: 〜ほうがいい
patterns.explanation: It would be better to — advice, not a command.

patterns.title: 〜つもり
patterns.explanation: Intends to, plans to — a decision already made.

patterns.title: 〜はず
patterns.explanation: Ought to be so, going by what the speaker knows.

patterns.title: 〜らしい
patterns.explanation: Apparently — reporting what the speaker has picked up from elsewhere.

patterns.title: 〜ばかり
patterns.explanation: Only that, nothing else — or, after a past form, that it has only just happened. Casually ばっかり or ばっか.

examples.japanese: 来たばかり。
examples.english: I only just got here.

patterns.title: 〜ために
patterns.explanation: For the sake of, or because of. Which one it is depends on what comes before it.

patterns.title: 〜なければならない
patterns.formation: negative provisional (〜なければ) + ならない
patterns.explanation: Must do it — there is no acceptable alternative. Literally: if you do not, it will not do.

examples.japanese: 行かなければならない。
examples.english: I have to go.

patterns.title: 〜てくる
patterns.explanation: The action comes toward the speaker, or has been building up until now.

patterns.title: 〜なん（な + の）
patterns.explanation: Setting up an explanation. な is the copula after a noun or な-adjective, and ん is の contracted — it turns what came before into the thing being explained. The copula after it carries the tense, politeness or negation.
patterns.detail: The plain form is 〜なのだ; なん is what it becomes in speech, and what a reader meets far more often. Compare 食べるんだ, where a verb needs no な because it can precede の on its own — the な here is doing the work a noun predicate requires.

examples.japanese: 学生なんだ。
examples.english: The thing is, he's a student.

examples.japanese: ここ、静かなんです。
examples.english: It's that this place is quiet.

patterns.title: 〜ていく
patterns.explanation: The action moves away from the speaker, or carries on from here.

patterns.title: 〜てしまう
patterns.explanation: It is done completely — often with regret that it happened.

patterns.title: 〜ておく
patterns.explanation: Do it in advance and leave it done, ready for later.

patterns.title: 〜てみる
patterns.explanation: Try doing it and see how it turns out.

patterns.title: 〜ている
patterns.explanation: It is going on right now, or the state it left behind continues.

patterns.title: 〜てある
patterns.explanation: Someone has done it, and it has been left that way on purpose.

patterns.title: 〜てくれる
patterns.explanation: Someone does it for the speaker, as a kindness.

patterns.title: 〜てもらう
patterns.explanation: The speaker gets someone else to do it for them.

patterns.title: 〜てあげる
patterns.explanation: The speaker does it for someone else's benefit.

patterns.title: なんて
patterns.explanation: Holds a thing or a whole situation up with surprise, disbelief or disdain — 'the likes of', 'that … should'. At the start of an exclamation (なんていい子) it means 'what a'.

examples.japanese: 君が失敗するなんて不思議だ。
examples.english: It is strange that you should fail.

examples.japanese: 豆腐がこんなにおいしいなんて知らなかった。
examples.english: I didn't know that tofu tasted this good.

patterns.title: 〜ごとに
patterns.explanation: Each and every — once for each one, or each time it happens; with time words, at that interval.

examples.japanese: ６時間ごとにこの薬を飲みなさい。
examples.english: Take this medicine every six hours.

examples.japanese: 彼女は日ごとに快方に向かっています。
examples.english: She is getting better day by day.

patterns.title: 〜おきに
patterns.explanation: At intervals, with that much left between each: 一日おきに is every other day. With minutes or metres it usually reads as 'every'.

examples.japanese: 母は１日おきに風呂に入る。
examples.english: My mother takes a bath every other day.

examples.japanese: バスは１０分おきに出ます。
examples.english: The bus leaves every 10 minutes.

patterns.title: 〜せいか
patterns.formation: plain clause / noun + の + せいか
patterns.explanation: Perhaps because — offers a cause without committing to it. 〜せいで states the cause outright.

examples.japanese: 暑くなってきたせいか、食品が傷むのが早い。
examples.english: Maybe because the weather's gotten hotter, the food is spoiling more quickly than usual.

examples.japanese: 飛行機でお酒飲むと、気圧のせいか酔いやすい。
examples.english: Maybe it's the low air pressure that means you get drunk more easily on planes.

patterns.title: 〜といえば
patterns.explanation: Speaking of — takes up a topic that has just come up, or names what something first brings to mind.

examples.japanese: 趣味といえば、あなたは切手を集めていますか。
examples.english: Speaking of hobbies, do you collect stamps?

examples.japanese: 彼らは日本といえば富士山を想像する。
examples.english: They often connect Japan with Mt. Fuji.

patterns.title: どちらかといえば / どちらかというと
patterns.explanation: If anything — leaning one way without committing to it.

examples.japanese: どちらかといえば彼の方が私より背が高い。
examples.english: He is, if anything, a little taller than I.

examples.japanese: 彼女はどちらかといえば今日は少しよくなっている。
examples.english: She is, if anything, a little better today.

patterns.title: なんだか
patterns.explanation: Somehow — the speaker feels it without being able to say why. Close to なんとなく, but more about the feeling itself.

examples.japanese: なんだか今日は声に元気がないね。何かあったの？
examples.english: Somehow you don't sound too good today. Is anything the matter?

examples.japanese: お前が怒ってる時ってさ、なんだか、かわいいな。
examples.english: You're kind of cute when you're mad.

patterns.title: なんとなく
patterns.explanation: Vaguely, for no reason one can name — a feeling, a hunch, or an understanding that is only partial.

examples.japanese: 中国語はなんとなくわかります。
examples.english: I more or less understand Chinese.

examples.japanese: 彼はなんとなく僕に恨みをもっているようだ。
examples.english: I don't know why, but he seems to have it in for me.

patterns.title: 〜とやら
patterns.explanation: Something called — names a thing the speaker only half knows, or repeats a name with a touch of doubt or irony.

examples.japanese: ふっ、禁断の魔術とやらは、俺には通用しないぜ！
examples.english: Hah, your 'forbidden magics' aren't going to work with me!

examples.japanese: 噂をすれば何とやら。キャシーが来たわよ。
examples.english: Speak of the devil, here comes Kathy.

patterns.title: 〜を余儀なくさせる
patterns.formation: noun + を余儀なくさせる
patterns.explanation: Forces it on someone — the cause is the subject, and what it imposes cannot be avoided. 〜を余儀なくされる says the same from the side of whoever was forced.

examples.japanese: その遅れは私たちに高級ホテルでの宿泊を余儀なくさせた。
examples.english: The delay forced us to stay overnight in an expensive hotel.

patterns.title: じゃん
patterns.explanation: Casual じゃない(か) at the end of a sentence: 'isn't it', 'you know' — inviting agreement, or pointing out something obvious.

examples.japanese: 声ガラガラじゃん。どうしたの？
examples.english: Your voice is raspy. Why?

examples.japanese: 待って、今日？次の金曜って言ってたじゃん！
examples.english: Wait, it's today? You told me it was next Friday!

patterns.title: 〜かな
patterns.explanation: I wonder — a question asked of oneself, softer than か alone. After a volitional (行こうかな) it is a decision half made.

examples.japanese: 私、トムの気持ち傷つけちゃったかな。
examples.english: I wonder if I hurt Tom's feelings.

examples.japanese: お天気いいし、散歩に行こうかな。
examples.english: It's a nice day and I feel like taking a walk.

patterns.title: 〜でしょ / 〜だろ
patterns.formation: plain form / noun + でしょ, だろ
patterns.explanation: Casual でしょう and だろう with the last sound dropped: 'right?', 'isn't it?' — pressing for agreement more than guessing.

examples.japanese: あんたには関係ないでしょ。
examples.english: Mind your own business.

examples.japanese: どう考えてもおかしいだろ。
examples.english: It's suspicious no matter how you think about it.

patterns.title: 〜とこ
patterns.explanation: Casual ところ — the place, or the point in time: 行くとこ is about to go, したとこ has just done it.

examples.japanese: トムの家に行くとこだよ。
examples.english: I'm on my way to Tom's.

examples.japanese: ちょうど洗車したとこだよ。
examples.english: I've just washed the car.

patterns.title: 〜まんま
patterns.explanation: Casual まま: just as it is, unchanged.

examples.japanese: トムはプロフィール写真のまんまだね。
examples.english: Tom looked exactly like his profile picture.

patterns.title: 〜なきゃ / 〜なくちゃ
patterns.formation: negative stem + なきゃ / なくちゃ
patterns.explanation: Casual 'have to', with the rest of 〜なければならない or 〜なくてはならない left unsaid.

examples.japanese: あ、もうこんな時間。行かなきゃ。
examples.english: Oh, it's already this late. I have to go.

examples.japanese: 家に帰らなくちゃ。
examples.english: I have to go home.

patterns.title: 〜かい / 〜だい
patterns.formation: plain form + かい; question word (+ の/ん) + だい
patterns.explanation: A casual question ending, mostly in men's or older speech: か softened with い, or だい after a question word (何だい, どうしたんだい).

examples.japanese: トム、君は幸せかい？
examples.english: Are you happy, Tom?

examples.japanese: 君の車どうしたんだい？
examples.english: What have you done with your car?

patterns.title: 〜って
patterns.explanation: Casual と, という or は: quotes what someone said (嫌だって言ってた), reports hearsay at the end of a sentence, or picks out a topic (あなたって…).

examples.japanese: あいつ、新しい仕事が嫌だって言ってたよ。
examples.english: He said he didn't like his new job.

examples.japanese: あなたって、本当に可愛いわね。
examples.english: You're really cute.

patterns.title: 〜たって
patterns.explanation: Casual 〜ても: even if, no matter how. 泣いたって is 泣いても.

examples.japanese: 泣いたってしょうがないだろ。
examples.english: Crying won't help.

examples.japanese: いくら走ったって、間に合わないって。
examples.english: No matter how much you run, you'll never make it on time.

patterns.title: 〜てはいけない
patterns.formation: te-form + は + いけない / ならない / だめ
patterns.explanation: Must not — literally 'if you do it, it won't do'. With a negative (〜なくてはいけない) it turns round into 'must'.

examples.japanese: あの男を信用してはいけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't trust that man.

examples.japanese: 口にものを入れたまま話してはいけません。
examples.english: Do not talk with your mouth full.

patterns.title: 〜ちゃだめ / 〜ちゃいけない
patterns.formation: te-form contracted to 〜ちゃ / 〜じゃ + だめ / いけない
patterns.explanation: Casual 'must not': 〜ちゃ is 〜ては contracted (〜じゃ after a voiced て), so 触っちゃ駄目 is 触ってはだめ.

examples.japanese: ペンキ塗りたてだから、触っちゃ駄目よ。
examples.english: Don't touch the wet paint.

examples.japanese: たき火で遊んじゃだめだよ。
examples.english: Don't play with open fire.
